subject: Dedicated capacity — oversubscription guardrails & traffic questionnaire
messages:
From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@aperture.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity for real-time summarization — quick snapshot attached

Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We want to explore a Redwood Dedicated deployment to power Aperture’s real-time meeting summarization bolt. A quick snapshot of our expected traffic is attached (aperture_traffic_snapshot.csv) and a small sample of prompts is in example_prompts.txt. High-level notes: 

- Workload: streaming transcription -> summarization in near-real-time (user-facing).
- Typical prompt tokens: median ~80 tokens (system + user), 95th ~240 tokens.
- Typical completion tokens: median ~280 tokens, 95th ~720 tokens.
- Baseline QPS target: 160 qps sustained across peak region; burst windows up to ~520 qps for ~3–7 minutes (market events).
- Latency target: p95 generation <= 350ms for the 90% workload; 99th should be best-effort but <1s if possible.
- We care a lot about tail behavior and cold-starts — KV cache priming is useful.
- Security: SOC2 + encrypted-at-rest; we may need VPC private deployment later.

Two asks: 1) How do you typically set oversubscription guardrails for bursty streaming workloads? 2) What specific fields do you need from us to produce a recommended Dedicated pool size and initial guardrails?

Can you review the snapshot and let us know if there are obvious missing pieces?

Sam
Head of Platform Engineering
Aperture Analytics

Attachments: aperture_traffic_snapshot.csv (csv), example_prompts.txt (txt)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@aperture.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for real-time summarization — quick snapshot attached

Sam — thanks for the snapshot and the clear numbers. I reviewed the CSV and the prompt samples; that's helpful. To produce a defensible Dedicated sizing and oversubscription plan we need a short structured response to the items below. If easier, happy to walk through on a 30-minute call — I can get Ben (solutions) and Marissa (AE) on.

Quick questionnaire (responses best-effort):
1) Peak sustained concurrency: what is the highest sustainable concurrent generation requests you expect over a 30–60 minute window? (e.g., 2,400 concurrent tokens-in-flight)
2) Burst profile: how often do bursts occur and typical burst duration? (you gave 3–7 min; approximate daily/weekly frequency helps)
3) Token distribution: confirm median/95/99 for both prompt and completion tokens (CSV looked like median prompt ~80 and median completion ~280 but we need exact percentiles).
4) Request mix: % streaming vs % non-streaming (batch/async) and % of requests that can tolerate >500ms latency.
5) Caching: can you prefix-cache identical prefixes or re-use KV caches across sessions? Any multi-turn reuse?
6) SLO classes: do you have multiple service tiers (e.g., interactive vs background) and what percent of traffic maps to each?
7) Model fidelity / quantization tolerance: would you accept a quantized variant for cost? Are you sensitive to small non-deterministic regressions?
8) Warm/idle constraints: how long can instances maintain KV cache state before you consider it stale?
9) Security/compliance constraints that affect placement/networking (VPC, on-prem, KMS).
10) Business runway: is this a pilot (1–3 months) or year-long committed Dedicated conversation?

A few things on our side: for streaming workloads we typically provision a low-latency tier (small pool) and an autoscaled best-effort tier; we place conservative guardrails at first (reserve ~20–30% headroom, limit oversubscription to 2.0–2.8x depending on model/token length) and then adjust after 2 weeks of telemetry. We also favor prefix/KV caching and pre-warming for predictable bursts.

If you can reply with the numbered items, we'll produce a recommended Dedicated configuration (pool size, GPU class guidance, oversubscription ratio per tier, warm cache sizing, and a rollout plan).

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@aperture.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for real-time summarization — quick snapshot attached

Karthik / Marissa — thanks, answers below. I attached a slightly expanded CSV and a short notes PDF on our security requirements (aperture_security_notes.pdf).

1) Peak sustained concurrency: we estimate ~1,900 concurrent active generations sustained for 45–60 minutes during business-critical trading windows.
2) Burst profile: bursts ~3–5x baseline occur about 2–4 times per week and last 3–10 minutes; monthly long-tail events up to ~12 minutes.
3) Token distribution (percentiles): Prompt: p50=78, p90=210, p95=240; Completion: p50=275, p90=520, p95=720, p99~1200.
4) Request mix: ~82% streaming (low-latency), ~18% async batch. ~92% of requests must be <=350ms p95; the remainder can be background.
5) Caching: we can reuse KV cache across sessions for recurring speakers and have about 25% prefix reuse; we cannot share user-specific private prefixes across customers.
6) SLO classes: single interactive tier (90% of traffic) + a small background tier.
7) Quantization tolerance: we can accept int8/4 quantization for background tier, interactive must be near-floating point parity.
8) Warm/idle: ideally KV cache retained for 20–30 minutes of idle to cover short pauses in conversations.
9) Security: SOC2, customer data residency in us-west-2, VPC peering required for production; KMS key for encrypting model keys.
10) Business runway: pilot first month, target committed 12-month Dedicated if numbers are good.

We'd like Redwood's recommended starting pool and guardrails so we can budget and align internal procurement cycles. Happy to hop on a call Wednesday afternoon PT.

Sam

Attachments: aperture_security_notes.pdf (pdf), aperture_traffic_snapshot_v2.csv (csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@aperture.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 18:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for real-time summarization — oversubscription & recommended kickoff

Sam — great data, thanks for the fast turnaround. Based on your distribution and the strict interactive SLOs, here’s a conservative starting recommendation from Redwood’s pre-sales sizing team (we'll refine after a 7–14 day telemetry window):

Preliminary proposal (pilot -> committed roadmap):
- Pilot Dedicated pool: 6 GPUs (low-latency tier) + 2 GPUs (background tier) — GPU class recommendation depends on model but expect equivalent of 80–110 TFLOP GPU-class for the interactive tier.
- Initial oversubscription guardrail: interactive tier = 2.2x, background tier = 4.0x. We keep 25% headroom for KV warm caches and cold-start spikes for the first month.
- KV cache sizing: allocate per-GPU cache budget to retain 20–30 minutes of active sessions; this reduces cold-start impact for your multi-turn flows.
- Routing policy: hard-route interactive traffic to low-latency pool; auto-fallback to background tier for non-critical requests when load > 85% sustained for 60s.
- Observability: we will instrument p50/p95/p99 token latencies, queueing time, and cache hit-rate; first dashboard shared within 48 hours of pilot start.
- Security: start with Dedicated in our us-west-2 region with VPC peering and bring-your-own-KMS integration; we'll prepare the SOC2 evidence bundle during onboarding.

Next steps / action items:
1) Confirm timing for a 30-min kickoff (we proposed Wed 4 PM PT or Thu 10 AM PT).
2) Share or approve a sandbox CIDR block for VPC peering and the KMS key alias.
3) Sign the pilot terms (I'll share a short SOW and pilot pricing sheet).

Ben will follow up with a draft SOW and a ballpark cost estimate for the pilot pool plus telemetry-based scaling plan. Karthik will set the preflight checklist and coordinate an on-call window for the launch day.

Thanks — we’ll also attach a short one-pager with these guardrails to the HubSpot deal.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
